observed_text: Relative energy (or inferred-T) fluctuations of a finite population scale as N^{-1/2}. There is no single universal N at which a thermometer starts working.
implied_text: The hardware is a large exchanging population. Required N is set by the stability of the reading against the instrument, not by a material constant.
description: Temperature requires a statistical buffer; collapse is gradual in 1/√N, not a connected-film or KV cliff.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack and the magnet latch cell.

observed_text: Equilibration clocks are medium-specific: collision time of order 10^{-10} s in standard air; phonon/electron exchange from picoseconds to nanoseconds in ordinary crystals. Radiative exchange is slower.
implied_text: Observation faster than the population’s exchange window returns a sequence of incomplete averages, not T.
description: The thermometer clock is the medium’s equilibration window; ordinary condensed samples have already finished on any mechanical or human clock.
notes: The numerical window is medium for any one sample and geometry. Do not treat 10^{-10} s as a universal machine clock.

observed_text: No latch holds T. Barriers elsewhere (Curie point, superconducting gap, melting) destroy or replace this average; they are not the resource that produces T.
implied_text: T is produced by exchange among contributors, not by a barrier that protects a written state.
description: Temperature has no energy barrier that stores a state.
value_text: no latch; exchange, not a barrier
notes: Negative latch spec. Melting, superconductivity, and permanent-magnet-latch own the replacements.

observed_text: A sample with only a handful of independent contributors does not present a stable reading: successive observations scatter.
implied_text: Too few contributors → scatter dominates the mean → no stable thermometer reading.
description: Under-populated averages fail gradually; there is no single N at which T switches off.

observed_text: A reading taken inside the exchange window, or on a subsystem that is not exchanging, is not the equilibrium T.
implied_text: Drive or observation faster than the averaging window is a clock failure of the family: the output is not T.
description: Observe inside the exchange window and the thermometer does not report T.

observed_text: With no exchange channel — no collisions, no radiation, no contact — two bodies do not converge to a shared reading.
implied_text: Zeroth-law contact is a resource. Isolation prevents a shared average.
description: Without an exchange channel the population cannot finish a common T.

observed_text: A body left in contact with a larger body, or isolated long enough, presents a single stable thermometer reading. Two bodies in contact converge; a third that matches the first matches the second.
implied_text: The stable product is one shared number T, and with it the conversion kT between that number and an energy scale.
description: T is the averaged output of the exchanging population, not a single-node property.
notes: k = 1.380649e-23 J/K is defined in SI, not an extracted machine constant. kT ≈ 4.14e-21 J at 300 K is arithmetic from that defined k.

observed_text: k = 1.380649e-23 J/K is defined in SI. The N^{-1/2} scatter is taken from ensemble formulae. No universal minimum N is measured.
implied_text: QSA takes the observed scatter and the measured equilibration time as buffer and clock. It does not derive k, or a minimum N, from node rules.
description: The statistical buffer is named as a class but not given a node-rule number. That is a gap, not a contradiction, and it recurs on every entry in this family.
value_text: k defined; no derived min N
notes: Treating the defined k as an extracted machine constant would over-claim.

observed_text: Relative fluctuation of the count in a sub-volume scales as N^{-1/2}. A cubic micrometre of standard-density air still holds ∼10^7 molecules. There is no single universal N at which pressure begins.
implied_text: P as a stable reading requires enough independent impacts in the gauge window that the mean is not scatter-dominated.
description: The count buffer is statistical and gradual in 1/√N. It is not the Knudsen cliff.
value_text: count scatter ∼ N^{-1/2}; no universal N
notes: A cube of side ∼λ still holds of order 10^3–10^4. Count scatter and Kn ≳ 1 are not the same cliff.

observed_text: Continuum hydrodynamics fails when Kn = λ/L is no longer small. The load-bearing cliff is Kn ≳ 1. λ is of order 65 nm in standard air and scales as 1/n.
implied_text: Continuum P(r) requires L ≳ λ. That length tracks density; it is tens of nanometres in standard air and centimetres to metres in a rough vacuum. It is not a material constant.
description: The spatial buffer is relative (λ/L), not a fixed nanometre stack.
notes: Slip around Kn ∼ 10^{-2}–10^{-1} is an engineering convention. Do not rewrite λ ∼ 65 nm as a universal hardware stack.

observed_text: Collision time τ ∼ λ/v̄ is of order 10^{-10} s in standard-density air and much longer once the gas is rarefied. Ordinary mechanical gauges sit far above this clock.
implied_text: A gauge that resolves individual hits, or a drive faster than local equilibration, sees a shot sequence rather than P.
description: Wall pressure is an average over the impact / collision window.
value_text: τ ∼ 10^{-10} s (standard air); longer when rarefied
notes: 10^{-10} s is a standard-air order of magnitude, not a universal clock.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. Operating resources are density, an equilibration window, and an apparatus larger than λ.
implied_text: Pressure is averaged momentum flux, not a stored configuration.
description: Ideal-gas pressure has no energy barrier that stores a state.
value_text: no latch; n, window, L ≳ λ
notes: Ionization removes the neutral population this envelope assumes. Cross-cite ionization-threshold.

observed_text: When Kn ≳ 1, continuum hydro and a local P field collapse; the wall load is a ballistic rain. Conventional bands put slip near Kn ∼ 10^{-2}–10^{-1} and free-molecular flow for Kn ≳ 1.
implied_text: L has dropped through λ, or n has been lowered until λ exceeds L. A free-molecular beam can still deliver a time-averaged force; it does not support sound as a local mode.
description: The continuum reading dies when the apparatus is no longer large compared with the mean free path.
notes: The exact Kn at which a given gauge is declared invalid is a convention; the existence of the λ/L ∼ 1 collapse is not. Speed of sound owns the continuum mode that requires Kn ≪ 1.

observed_text: N too small in the sampled volume or window → the manometer reading jitters and P = nkT is not a stable output.
implied_text: Same 1/√N count buffer as the temperature entry, now on the wall-load average.
description: Too few independent impacts and the pressure reading is scatter, not P = nkT.
notes: Cross-cite thermal-equilibrium-temperature. Virial / liquid corrections at high density are a different envelope, not this Knudsen or count failure.

observed_text: A dilute gas in a closed vessel exerts a steady, uniform wall load P = nkT (or PV = NkT).
implied_text: The stable output is the averaged wall load P = nkT and, when Kn is small, a continuum hydrodynamic field built from that average.
description: Ideal-gas pressure is the averaged momentum transfer of a thermal population onto a wall.
notes: k is defined. Do not extract k as a machine constant. Ideal-gas P and continuum hydro are not the same artifact; this entry owns the wall load and the Kn failure.

observed_text: QSA does not derive k or the hard-sphere molecular diameter from node rules. The Knudsen buffer is relative (λ/L), not a fixed nanometre stack.
implied_text: Both k and molecular size are taken from the descriptive relations and from sizes measured elsewhere.
description: The relative path buffer is located; k and d are not derived. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
value_text: k and d taken; no universal L
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: A cavity so small or so cold that only a few electromagnetic modes sit under the thermal envelope does not present the smooth Planck shape. There is no single universal cavity size; the required volume tracks λ_max(T).
implied_text: Mode occupancy under the curve must be large enough, after averaging, to trace u(ν,T) rather than a handful of discrete lines, and the cavity must be large compared with the wavelengths that carry the energy at that T.
description: The hardware is a densely occupied thermal electromagnetic mode set coupled to a wall that itself has a stable T. No universal volume is extracted.
value_text: many modes; size ≳ λ_max(T); no universal V
notes: At 300 K the relevant wavelengths are tens of micrometres; at a few kelvin they are millimetres. Do not invent a universal cavity volume.

observed_text: Mode occupancy is of order one when hν ∼ kT. With defined h and k, kT/h ≈ 6.25 THz at 300 K. Optical frequencies at room temperature sit deep in the Wien tail. Wall thermalization must also finish.
implied_text: Frequencies well below kT/h sit in the Rayleigh–Jeans envelope; frequencies well above it are exponentially empty. A wall that has not finished exchanging does not emit a single-T spectrum.
description: The spectral clock is the defined ratio kT/h plus the wall exchange window.
notes: h and k are defined. 6.25 THz is arithmetic at 300 K, not an extracted machine clock.

observed_text: No latch. A metal wall that reflects in the optical is simply not black: ε(ν)<1 and the emitted spectrum is not Planck.
implied_text: That is a failure of the black-body boundary condition, not a stored state.
description: The blackbody spectrum has an operating boundary condition (ε=1), not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Cross-cite plasma-frequency-cutoff and reflection for why a metal wall is not black in the optical.

observed_text: Cavity modes under-populated, or size ≲ λ_max(T), give a discrete or suppressed spectrum. The output is not a Planck curve of a well-defined T.
implied_text: Under-occupied modes or a cavity not large compared with the Wien band collapse the smooth spectral average.
description: Few-mode or undersized cavities fail the Planck output for the same statistical reason a small N fails T.
notes: Wien λ_max T ≈ 2898 μm·K locates the band; that product follows defined h, c, k and is not a QSA extraction.

observed_text: A surface that is not black (polished metal, selective coating) emits a distorted, lower curve. ε(ν)≠1 → grey or selective emission; the shape is no longer universal.
implied_text: The wall has failed the black boundary condition. The same metal can succeed as a mirror and fail as a blackbody.
description: Non-black surfaces do not emit the universal Planck curve.
notes: Photoemission from the same hot wall is a different machine (photoelectric-threshold, work-function-thermionic).

observed_text: If the wall population itself has no stable T — too few contributors, or observation inside its exchange window — there is no thermal spectrum to emit.
implied_text: The spectrum inherits the temperature entry’s collapse: no stable wall average, no Planck curve.
description: An undefined wall T removes the thermal electromagnetic output.
value_text: wall T not a stable average
notes: Cross-cite thermal-equilibrium-temperature.

observed_text: A heated black cavity or surface emits a smooth spectrum that depends only on T. The per-wavelength peak follows Wien’s displacement; the frequency integral is the Stefan–Boltzmann law (other entry).
implied_text: The Planck curve u(ν,T) and its Wien peak, depending only on T, are the averaged spectral output of the thermal electromagnetic population.
description: The machine’s stable product is the measured Planck shape, not a derived occupation factor.
notes: h and k are defined. Relabel the measured curve; do not extract h as a QSA machine constant. Rayleigh–Jeans is a failed high-ν envelope, not an observed output. Integral owned by stefan-boltzmann.

observed_text: Real cavities have shape-dependent density-of-states corrections (Weyl terms, cutoffs), measured in micromachined and cryogenic resonators. The mapping does not derive h or the Planck occupation factor from node rules.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured curve and the Wien product as the output specification. Mode count is the buffer; those corrections confirm that without supplying a single universal volume.
description: h is taken, not derived, and there is no universal cavity volume. That is the same honest limit as the missing N on the temperature entry.
value_text: h taken; no universal cavity volume
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: The surface must present ε≈1 across the Wien band, and the radiating object must be large compared with λ_max(T), or the output is not σT^4. There is no single universal size cliff; the required area tracks T.
implied_text: Same statistical electromagnetic population as the blackbody spectrum, now read as one integrated current. Small or few-mode objects fall off the T^4 envelope for the same reason a sparse cavity falls off the Planck curve.
description: The hardware is a black-enough, large-enough radiator. No universal area is extracted.
value_text: ε≈1 on Wien band; size ≳ λ_max(T); no universal area
notes: At 300 K, λ_max ∼ 10 μm. Finite-size and near-field corrections are real; they do not yield a single area number.

observed_text: No separate clock beyond the wall-equilibration window and the spectral content already fixed by kT/h. The T^4 law is a time-averaged power.
implied_text: A detector faster than the wall exchange, or a surface whose T is not itself stable, does not report σT^4.
description: The T^4 reading inherits the wall averaging window and the spectral clock of the Planck curve.
notes: Clock inherited from blackbody-spectrum and thermal-equilibrium-temperature. k and h are defined.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. A high-reflectivity metal is a resource failure of the black boundary condition (ε collapsed), not a stored configuration.
implied_text: Low ε is not a memory. The operating condition is a black (or grey) surface, not a barrier.
description: Stefan–Boltzmann has a black-boundary operating condition, not an energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: Cross-cite reflection.

observed_text: Surface not black (ε(ν)≠1 across the Wien band) → reduced or non-T^4 output. A grey surface still follows T^4 with a reduced prefactor; a selective surface does not.
implied_text: The extra collapse of the integral is a boundary-condition failure of the same electromagnetic population, not a new machine.
description: Non-black or selective surfaces take the power meter off σT^4.
notes: The same surface can be nearly black in the thermal infrared and reflective in the visible.

observed_text: Object or cavity not large compared with λ_max(T), or modes under-populated → the integral of a non-Planck spectrum is not σT^4. Finite-size / diffraction corrections appear in that regime.
implied_text: Area and λ_max are the spatial resources of the integral, for the same reason a sparse cavity leaves the Planck curve.
description: Undersized radiators fall off the T^4 envelope.
notes: Cross-cite blackbody-spectrum. No universal area is attached.

observed_text: As T→0 the radiated power vanishes into the instrument floor. Net exchange between two black surfaces is σ(T1^4−T2^4).
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the photon current disappears. An undefined wall T is the same inherited collapse as the temperature entry.
description: T→0, or an unstable wall T, kills the T^4 reading.
notes: At 300 K, σT^4 ≈ 459 W m^{-2} is arithmetic from defined σ, not a machine number.

observed_text: A hot black surface radiates a hemispherical exitance j = εσT^4. Doubling T multiplies the exitance by sixteen.
implied_text: The T^4 exitance is the power-meter reading of a black thermal surface — the frequency integral of the Planck curve.
description: Relabel the T^4 law as the integrated output of the thermal electromagnetic population. The prefactor is not a QSA extraction.
notes: σ = 5.670374e-8 W m^{-2} K^{-4} is defined from h, k, and c. Extracting σ as an independent machine constant would double-count those defined constants.

observed_text: σ = 2π^5 k^4/(15 c^2 h^3) is a combination of defined constants. Finite-size corrections confirm that area and λ_max are the spatial resources and do not yield a single universal area.
implied_text: The mapping’s job is the T^4 envelope and its failures, not a re-derivation of the prefactor.
description: σ is defined; no universal radiating area is extracted. That is inherited from the spectrum entry.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Thermionic emission from the same hot surface is a charged-particle gate, not this photon-current integral.

observed_text: Free-electron Fermi temperatures: Cu 8.16e4 K, Ag 6.38e4 K, Al 13.6e4 K. The participating fraction T/T_F is 0.37 % for Cu at 300 K. There is no count at which electronic heat capacity begins.
implied_text: The hardware is the T-dependent Fermi-surface population of order (T/T_F)N, not a fixed node count. A metal with no Fermi surface has no such population at any N.
description: Electronic heat capacity uses a shrinking statistical slice, not a single buffer size.
value_text: ∼(T/T_F)N; T_F = 6.4e4–13.6e4 K (Ag, Cu, Al, free-electron model)
notes: Fermi temperatures are free-electron model values, not measurements.

observed_text: Electron–lattice energy transfer in thin copper films takes 1–4 ps, increasing with laser fluence.
implied_text: The relevant energy scale is kT against E_F, or against a gap Δ when one is present.
description: Calorimetry reads an already-finished electronic average.
notes: One metal measured. Heat deposited faster than this is held first by about 1 % of the heat capacity.

observed_text: The operating condition is no gap at the Fermi energy. In aluminium below Tc = 1.163 K the linear term is replaced by a roughly exponential one.
implied_text: The operating condition is an ungapped Fermi surface. The gaps that kill γT are owned by other families; they appear here only as the threshold that removes the average.
description: γT requires an open Fermi surface, not a latching barrier.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity and semiconductor-gap-absorption.

observed_text: γT falls linearly to zero in the normal state; aluminium follows C = γT + βT³ from 4.0 K down to 0.11 K. Above 3.8 K (Cu) or 7.4 K (Al) the lattice term is the larger; at 300 K the electronic share is 0.85 % (Cu), 1.7 % (Al), and about 6 % and 8 % (Fe, Ni, extrapolated).
implied_text: The average is still defined; the output is no longer a usable reading. The slice has shrunk, not gapped.
description: Cooling a normal metal sends γT into the calorimeter noise without a gap-closure event.
value_text: γT ∝ T; equal to lattice term at 3.8 K (Cu), 7.4 K (Al)
notes: Linear, with no critical value. The Fe and Ni shares assume the low-temperature γ holds to 300 K.

observed_text: In aluminium (Tc = 1.163 K) the superconducting electronic heat capacity for 0.25 < T/Tc < 0.5 follows C_es/γTc = 7.1 exp(−1.34 Tc/T), 13 % of the normal value at Tc/4; below that it lies above the exponential, by a factor of 4 at the lowest temperature. The heat capacity jumps at Tc.
implied_text: The contributing Fermi-surface slice has been removed, not merely cooled. This entry owns that the gap kills γT, not the gap itself.
description: A superconducting gap replaces the linear electronic heat capacity with an exponentially small remnant.
value_text: T < Tc: γT replaced by ∼exp(−1.34 Tc/T) (Al)
notes: A phase transition at Tc. Cross-cite superconductivity.

observed_text: A material with a gap at the Fermi energy has no metallic γT. No number is filed.
implied_text: Without a contributing slice at E_F there is no electronic linear term at any N or T.
description: No Fermi surface, no γT. That is a missing population, not a cooled metal.
notes: A property of the material class; no opened source was used. Cross-cite semiconductor-gap-absorption.

observed_text: C = γT + βT³ at low temperature. γ in mJ/mol K²: Cu 0.690–0.696, Ag 0.645–0.652, Al 1.35, Fe 4.89–4.90, Ni 7.04, Pd 9.42–9.45; CeAl3 1620. Free-electron values: Cu 0.505, Ag 0.645, Al 0.912.
implied_text: A heat capacity linear in T, with a material coefficient γ, is the averaged energy uptake of the Fermi-surface slice.
description: The stable output is C_e = γT. γ is taken from measurement, not derived here.
value_text: C_e = γT; γ = 0.65 (Ag) to 9.4 (Pd) mJ/mol K²; CeAl3 1620
notes: Ni rests on a compiled handbook page. Measured over free-electron: 1.38 (Cu), 1.00 (Ag), 1.48 (Al).

observed_text: γ is taken from measurement. The free-electron estimate is right for Ag and low by a factor of 1.4–1.5 for Cu and Al; in Pd the measured value is 1.7 times the band value.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured γ (or D(E_F), or T_F) as the material specification.
description: γ is located as a material coefficient and is not derived from node count.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. k is defined.

observed_text: Two nested statistical scales, neither a single cliff. The fluid must itself be a large thermal population with a stable T and, for Stokes drag, a continuum mean free path short compared with the particle. Visible jitter is the failure of the impact average to finish. There is no universal radius.
implied_text: Everyday stillness is the completed average; Brownian motion is the under-averaged remainder. “Visible” tracks optical resolution, T, η, and the chosen window.
description: No universal particle size is extracted. Making the tracer larger completes the average rather than crossing a hardware cliff.
value_text: no universal radius; bath continuum (L ≳ λ)
notes: A micrometre “cliff” because that is where a microscope works would be a convention, not a hardware threshold. D falls as 1/a; that is a scaling of the output, not an N-cliff.

observed_text: Momentum relaxation τ_p = m/γ is tens of nanoseconds for a micrometre sphere in water. Windows longer than τ_p see the overdamped random walk; shorter windows resolve ballistic segments.
implied_text: Two clocks: bath collision time, and tracer velocity-forget time τ_p. The overdamped MSD law is a clock constraint, not a different effect.
description: The overdamped Einstein walk applies only after the tracer has forgotten its momentum.
value_text: τ_p ∼ tens of ns (μm sphere in water)
notes: Tens of ns is a class for that tracer/bath, not a universal clock.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. The operating resource is kT against the drag. T→0 sends D→0. Removing the bath (vacuum) removes the impact rain.
implied_text: Jitter is not a stored configuration.
description: Brownian motion has no energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: k is defined.

observed_text: A particle so large, heavy, or overdamped that the kicks average below the resolution of the window looks still. D falls as 1/a. Everyday objects present no visible wander on the same window.
implied_text: This is completion of the average — collapse of the visible effect, not a missing machine.
description: When the impact average finishes inside the observation window, the named jitter disappears and the object looks still.
notes: Keep this explicit or the collapse statement looks like a missing machine rather than a finished one.

observed_text: Cooling the bath reduces the wander. T→0 sends D→0.
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the incomplete mechanical average disappears.
description: No thermal bath energy, no Einstein diffusivity.
notes: Shares this collapse with johnson-nyquist-noise (4kTRΔf).

observed_text: Windows ≪ τ_p resolve ballistic segments. The overdamped ⟨x^2⟩ = 2dDt envelope does not apply there.
implied_text: Clock constraint on the overdamped output, not a different machine.
description: Observe faster than momentum relaxation and the Einstein walk is the wrong envelope.
notes: Optical-tweezer experiments resolve this crossover. Knudsen or vacuum conditions separately fail Stokes γ and the Einstein relation in the form above.

observed_text: D = kT/γ and ⟨x^2⟩ = 2dDt for t ≫ τ_p. For a micrometre sphere in water, D is of order 10^{-13} m^2 s^{-1}, so the rms displacement in one second is of order a micrometre.
implied_text: Diffusivity and a linearly growing MSD are the still-visible remainder of an incomplete impact average. For large bodies the emergent output on the same window is stillness.
description: The named output is the Einstein relation, the electrical twin of which is 4kTRΔf.
notes: k is defined. Do not extract 10^{-13} m^2 s^{-1} as a universal machine number; it is a class for a micrometre tracer in water. Cross-cite johnson-nyquist-noise.

observed_text: The mapping does not derive k or Stokes’ 6π from node rules. There is no single particle-size cliff.
implied_text: QSA takes D = kT/γ and the measured τ_p crossover as the specifications. The missing universal radius is the same statistical gap as the missing N on the temperature entry.
description: k and the Stokes prefactor are taken; no universal tracer size is extracted.
value_text: k and 6π taken; no universal a
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: There is no universal resistor volume at which 4kTRΔf starts working. A lithographed nanometre-scale resistor still presents the Nyquist floor once it has a well-defined R and a bath T. Extra noise in small devices is shot, telegraph, or two-level-system, not a missing thermal floor.
implied_text: The hardware is a dissipative element with stable R, coupled to a thermal population with stable T, averaged over the chosen Δf. Inventing a minimum N of carriers would be a conjecture.
description: Johnson–Nyquist names a statistical average and does not attach a resistor-volume cliff.
notes: 1/f and TLS noise sit on top of the Nyquist floor; they are a different output, not the collapse of this effect.

observed_text: Two clocks: observation bandwidth Δf, and the thermal electromagnetic / electronic clock kT/h (≈ 6.25 THz at 300 K; tens of gigahertz at a few kelvin). The classical envelope fails when hf is no longer small compared with kT.
implied_text: Narrowing Δf is a longer average and kills the integrated variance. Drive or observation above kT/h leaves the classical Nyquist formula for the high-frequency envelope.
description: Classical 4kTR is an averaging-window statement below kT/h.
notes: h and k are defined. 6.25 THz is arithmetic, not an extracted machine clock. Ordinary audio and RF sit far below kT/h at 300 K; cryogenic microwave work does not.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. Sending the resistor into the superconducting state (R→0) removes the voltage noise by removing R.
implied_text: Noise is the electrical average of a dissipative element, not a stored configuration.
description: Johnson–Nyquist has no energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity for the R→0 realization.

observed_text: T→0 → ⟨V^2⟩→0 in the Nyquist formula. Cooling the resistor toward T=0 kills the classical noise.
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the electrical average vanishes.
description: Classical Johnson noise collapses as T→0.
notes: Shares this collapse with brownian-motion (D = kT/γ). Zero-point bookkeeping at T=0 is omitted; see the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: Δf→0 → integrated variance → 0. A measurement taken in a vanishing bandwidth is quiet. The spectral density may still be 4kTR; the reading of a zero-width filter is not a noise power.
implied_text: Lengthen the average until the variance is gone. That is the family clock failure run on the filter.
description: Vanishing bandwidth collapses the integrated Nyquist variance.

observed_text: R→0 → voltage noise → 0 (a short). A superconductor below T_c is the clean material realization of that limit. R→∞ (open) collapses current noise instead.
implied_text: Remove the dissipative resource and the voltage floor collapses.
description: A short, including a superconductor, has no Johnson voltage noise.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity. Skin effect retunes the R(f) that Nyquist consumes; it does not replace Nyquist.

observed_text: Classical Nyquist envelope ⟨V^2⟩ = 4kTRΔf. At 300 K a 1 kΩ resistor delivers ≈ 4.07 nV Hz^{-1/2}; a 50 Ω resistor delivers ≈ 0.91 nV Hz^{-1/2}.
implied_text: A white voltage floor 4kTR is the electrical average of the thermal population, with a definite integrated variance once Δf is stated.
description: The stable output is the Nyquist floor. It is the electrical fluctuation–dissipation twin of D = kT/γ.
notes: k is defined. The nV Hz^{-1/2} figures are arithmetic at 300 K, not extracted machine constants. Cross-cite brownian-motion.

observed_text: The mapping does not supply a resistor-volume cliff, and the data do not demand one. The high-frequency form is kept as an envelope; whether an hf/2 term is an available voltage on a given bench is not settled by this entry.
implied_text: Zero-point arguments about what a voltmeter can extract at T=0 are omitted. That is a recorded gap in interpretation, not a gap in the T→0 / Δf→0 collapse class.
description: No volume cliff is extracted, and zero-point voltage is not filed as a QSA output.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: A population of moments free to follow the field and sharing a bath temperature. χ is the averaged response; no minimum count is defined. One mole of S = 1/2, g = 2 moments has a Curie constant of 0.375 cm³ K/mol.
implied_text: Macro χ is the averaged response of the unlocked population. Dilute moments still follow Curie once N is large enough for the magnetometer; concentrated moments follow Curie–Weiss until they lock.
description: Curie paramagnetism is a statistical unlocked-moment average. No spin-count cliff and no KV volume threshold are extracted.
value_text: no universal N; volume is count, not KV
notes: Contrast with permanent-magnet-latch and superparamagnetism (a grain with a KV barrier and a retention-time crossover).

observed_text: Single moments precess at 28.02 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). The Curie reading is a time average of the projection along the field. No relaxation time is filed.
implied_text: Observation faster than the bath exchange, or faster than the moment’s relaxation in the host, is not χ = C/T.
description: χ = C/T is an average over the host / bath relaxation window, not a single-spin precession readout.
notes: 28.025 GHz/T is the single-spin carrier owned as a clock by permanent-magnet-latch. Do not treat it as a Curie-law number.

observed_text: No barrier holds the moments: the magnetization curve of Cr³⁺ alum follows the reversible Brillouin function to 99.5 % of saturation, with no remanence at zero field.
implied_text: This machine exists only while there is no anisotropy barrier holding a remnant. Soft iron above its useful coercivity but below T_C is still a ferromagnetic collective, not Curie.
description: Curie paramagnetism requires the absence of the magnet-latch barrier.
value_text: no latch; unlocked moments; zero remnant at B=0
notes: Contrast with permanent-magnet-latch. Ferromagnetic-hysteresis owns the poorly latched ferromagnet. Superparamagnetism is a small grain with a KV barrier that only looks unlocked above T_B.

observed_text: Above the ordering temperature χ = C/(T − θ) (mean field); the form fails close to the Curie point, and below it the ferromagnet has a spontaneous magnetization.
implied_text: χ = C/T dies because the machine has changed family — unlocked ensemble replaced by latched or staggered order — not because this average was merely cooled.
description: Order at T_C / T_N / θ replaces the Curie ensemble with a different machine.
notes: A phase transition. Ordering temperatures are filed on the ordered-state entries.

observed_text: μ_B/k = 0.6717 K/T, so μ_B B = kT at 447 T (300 K) and 1.49 T (1 K). Cr³⁺ alum reaches 99.5 % of saturation at 1.29 K and 5 T, following the Brillouin function (99.6 % computed) and not the Langevin function. At 1 T and 300 K the same ion is at 0.37 % of saturation.
implied_text: Above μB ∼ kT the Brillouin function saturates and χ is no longer C/T.
description: Large B/T takes the unlocked population out of the linear Curie envelope without locking it.
value_text: M/M_sat = B_J(gμ_B J B/kT); 99.5 % at 5 T and 1.29 K
notes: A function of B/T with no critical field.

observed_text: χ = C/T falls without limit as T rises; the law itself holds at high temperature and weak field.
implied_text: High-T collapse of the useful moment is still Curie, just an unusably small average.
description: χ = C/T remains the envelope as T→∞, but the useful moment for a given B disappears.
notes: Continuous, 1/T. Not a change of family.

observed_text: χ = C/T, an experimental fit valid at high temperature and weak field, with C = μ0 n g² μ_B² J(J+1)/3k for non-interacting moments; C/(T − θ) with interactions. Zero remanence at zero field.
implied_text: Reversible susceptibility is the averaged projection of an unlocked-moment population. Remanence at B=0 is the latch, not this average.
description: The stable output is χ = C/T with zero remnant. That is the unlocked contrast to the latched magnet.
notes: Pauli paramagnetism of a metal goes to a constant at low temperature and is not filed as Curie.

observed_text: C and θ are taken from fits or from the ionic configuration; the mapping does not compute them and names no minimum spin count.
implied_text: C and θ are taken from measurement. Those are the same honest gaps as on the other ensemble-average entries.
description: C and θ are taken, not derived, and no universal moment count is extracted.
value_text: C, θ taken; no universal N
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. k is defined.

observed_text: Mean free path in copper at room temperature is 39–40 nm. A film of thickness d has ρ = ρ0[1 + (3/8)(Λ0/d)(1 − p)] in the thick-film form; grain boundaries add to it, and measured copper films rise faster than the surface term with p = 0 predicts.
implied_text: The bulk constant is an average over many scattering events. It holds when every dimension of the conductor and of its grains is large against the mean free path; below that it rises continuously.
description: Resistivity needs a statistical buffer: dimensions large against the mean free path.
notes: The surface term adds 37.5 % at d = Λ0 with p = 0, at the edge of the thick-film form. Fuchs (1938), Sondheimer (1952) and Mayadas and Shatzkes (1970) were not opened. The size dependence is a crossover with no minimum size.

observed_text: Specific action g = ∫J² dt; the energy deposited is the integral of resistivity over g. At 1e10 A/m² melting begins after g/J² = 0.81 ms in copper, 0.25 ms in aluminium and 0.13 ms in iron. The scattering time of the carriers in copper at 293 K is 2.46e-14 s.
implied_text: Two clocks. The scattering time is the averaging window of the carriers. The heating clock is the action integral, which runs at J².
description: Joule heating is clocked by the action integral ∫J² dt.
value_text: t = g/J²; Cu 0.81 ms at 10 kA/mm²
notes: One 1975 data set on 0.1 mm wires. Under a pulse the current density of the surface layer enters g, not the total current over the full cross-section (skin-effect).

observed_text: Conduction in a bulk metal is a driven dissipative average with a heating rate ρJ² per unit volume. Steps in the resistivity occur at melting, at the oxide film of a powder contact and at a superconducting transition.
implied_text: No barrier holds a state. The gates that appear as steps belong to melting, electrical-contacts and superconductivity.
description: Resistivity has no energy barrier of its own; its steps are borrowed thresholds.
notes: Negative latch spec.

observed_text: ρ = ρ0 + ρi(T), with ρi ∝ T above the Debye temperature and T⁵ well below it. Near 293 K the coefficient is 0.0038–0.0044 per K in Ag, Cu, W and Al and 0.0054–0.0056 per K in Fe and Ni. IACS copper is defined with 0.00393 per °C.
implied_text: The room-temperature constant drifts continuously with the thermal population of the lattice. There is no critical temperature below melting; Fe and Ni change slope at the Curie point without a step.
description: Resistivity rises continuously with temperature, about 0.4 % per kelvin in copper.
notes: Coefficients are slopes between the 273 K and 300 K table rows. The 0.00160 per °C listed for steel 1020 in IEEE Std 80 is a constant of that standard's fusing formula, not a measured slope. Bloch–Grüneisen is derived for a special model.

observed_text: At the melting point the resistivity steps up: copper 10.171 → 21.01e-8 Ω·m at 1357.6 K (ratio 2.07), silver 2.06, aluminium 2.34, nickel 1.37, iron 1.055. Exploding-wire data give 1.91 for copper and 1.04 for iron.
implied_text: Loss of lattice order changes the scattering population at a definite temperature. The solid-state constant ends there.
description: Resistivity steps at the melting point; the size of the step is material-specific.
notes: The transition is owned by melting; this row records the resistivity step. Liquid values for Cu and Ni are provisional. The two sources disagree for tungsten (1.08 against 1.29). Do not equate Tm with other thermal thresholds.

observed_text: Specific action at the start of melting in 0.1 mm wires: Cu 8.05e16, Ag 6.17e16, Al 2.52e16, W 2.43e16, Ni 1.72e16, Fe 1.28e16 A²·s/m⁴. Burst follows at 2.1–2.8 times that and rises with current density. No value was found for any steel.
implied_text: The solid conductor has an action budget. The integral is continuous; the threshold is the phase change it reaches.
description: Joule heating ends the solid conductor at a material-specific action.
notes: One data set (1975); a 2013 study reporting disagreement for Cu and Al was seen only as a snippet. The adiabatic model with IEEE Std 80 constants gives 1.57e16 for steel 1020, 23 % above pure iron wire. Burst is rate-dependent and is not a material constant.

observed_text: A powder compact follows ρE = ρres(1 − Θ/ΘM)^(−n), diverging at the tap porosity ΘM; n = 3/2 without oxide and 1.5–3.6 as fitted. Pressed copper compacts measure 1e4–1e5 Ω·m unreduced, about 1e12 times bulk, and 1e-5–1e-6 Ω·m or less after the oxide is reduced at 190–210 °C in forming gas. No value was found for loose or oil-borne copper powder.
implied_text: A granular conductor needs a connected path through contacts whose surface films conduct. Past the percolation bound, or with insulating films, the bulk constant does not apply.
description: A powder body conducts only on the dense side of its percolation bound and only through reduced contacts.
notes: The copper-compact figures were read from a graph; the reduced value is the floor of the plot, at most 60–600 times bulk. Under pressure alone the resistance follows a power law, a crossover. Contact physics is owned by electrical-contacts.

observed_text: Resistivity at 293 K in 1e-8 Ω·m: Ag 1.587, Cu 1.678, Al 2.650, W 5.28, Ni 6.93, Fe 9.61. The ratio κ/σT is 2.12–2.90e-8 V²/K² at 273 K against the Sommerfeld value 2.443e-8.
implied_text: An intensive constant ρ(T) independent of sample shape above the mean-free-path scale, a heating rate ρJ² per unit volume, and a ratio to thermal conductivity within about 20 % of L0·T.
description: The averaged carrier population emits one material constant that sets both the voltage drop and the heating.
notes: IACS copper (1.7241e-8 Ω·m) is a convention for commercial metal. Low-carbon steel at 14.3–15.9e-8 Ω·m rests on a design standard and a vendor sheet.

observed_text: The Lorenz ratio deviates from the Sommerfeld value by up to about 20 % at ordinary temperatures. Matthiessen's rule has measured deviations. The resistivity of a powder body is set by contact films that are described only by a fitted residual resistivity and exponent.
implied_text: The mapping does not reduce the difference between the charge and heat averages, or the contact state of a granular body, to a buffer or clock number.
description: Bulk resistivity closes as an ensemble average; the Lorenz deviations and the powder contact state remain open.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.
